one_line: Parametric 3D vessel designs become precise printable clay templates with human-agent collaboration.
what_it_does: Lets an agent change vessel parameters while the app deterministically generates unfolded, multipage templates for pottery construction.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP provides structured parameter control and shared reversible state for a geometry workflow where generic UI driving would be less reliable; deterministic export is the key product boundary.
leverage_evidence: Transcript describes paired ChatGPT/browser state syncing in under one second.
Transcript says human and agent changes share undo/redo.
Devpost screenshot shows a measured 3D vessel beside its unfolded template.
Pitch explicitly separates agent complexity handling from deterministic template generation.
execution_rationale: The packet coherently shows a parametric editor concept, measured vessel geometry, and corresponding template, with a live demo claimed alive, but the visual packet is primarily video/packaging evidence rather than independently observed export.
execution_evidence: 179-second demo transcript describes parameter changes and template generation.
Frame sheets show vessel previews, dimension annotations, and template forms.
Devpost page embeds a titled WebMCP demo.
impact_rationale: Potters and makers have a concrete need for accurate, buildable templates; avoiding failed cuts after hours of studio work is a credible niche impact.
impact_evidence: About text identifies pottery template failures and misaligned PDFs as the problem.
Pitch targets buildable clay templates with precise geometry.
creativity_rationale: The combination of conversational design intent, parametric 3D vessels, and deterministic physical craft templates is a fresh and memorable WebMCP use.
creativity_evidence: Product bridges AI shape exploration and printable pottery construction.
Human-agent collaboration and reversible edits are pursued as core interaction design.
usability_note: Clear division between agent exploration and human parameter control/export; pairing flow adds some setup friction.
standouts: Deterministic physical output is a strong reason to expose structured tools.
Undo/redo across human and agent edits is thoughtful shared-state design.
advance_reason: Strong WebMCP delta and credible, distinctive craft workflow with substantial demonstrated coherence.

one_line: Turns scientific papers into auditable, rerunnable agent-operable evidence workspaces.
what_it_does: Exposes typed tools for manifests, provenance, deterministic analyses, sensitivity checks, claim rules, figures, audit trails, and human-approved evidence updates.
leverage_rationale: The paper itself becomes a structured scientific tool surface; this materially changes agent access from reconstructing prose/PDFs to bounded reruns, provenance inspection, and shared rendered results.
leverage_evidence: Transcript says 15 typed WebMCP tools come directly from the page, not table scraping or a copied notebook.
Transcript describes bounded reruns, claim evaluation, rendered forest plots, and SHA-256 input/result receipts.
Frames show manifests, forest plots, audit/provenance panels, and evidence maps.
execution_rationale: All major surfaces agree and the long demo transcript describes an end-to-end workflow with explicit limitations, human approval, provenance, analysis, and evidence mapping.
execution_evidence: 170-second transcript covers inspection, claim challenge, rerun, sensitivity plot, ledger, authoring, approval, and multilingual evidence map.
Frames show structured extraction fields, risk-of-bias data, plots, workbench, and audit controls.
Devpost screenshot visibly shows source locators, quotes, derivations, estimates, and bias fields.
impact_rationale: Researchers, reviewers, and evidence synthesists have a serious problem with unverifiable claims and expensive reproduction; this directly lowers inspection and challenge cost while preserving human governance.
impact_evidence: About text identifies AI reconstruction errors and costly verification as the problem.
Demo handles a historical meta-analysis with 19 records across 18 experiments and explicit provenance/risk-of-bias tracking.
creativity_rationale: The concept of an executable, cross-examinable paper with bounded agent operations and human-governed evidence admission is unusually original and pursued deeply.
creativity_evidence: Scientific document is treated as an agent-operable tool surface rather than static prose.
Evidence board generalizes beyond meta-analysis while preserving original-language quotes.
usability_note: Structured workflow and explicit caveats support trust; research concepts and many controls may be demanding for casual readers.
red_flags: Benchmark section explicitly has zero runs, so no speed or accuracy claim is evidenced.
standouts: Strong evidence honesty: reproducibility is explicitly separated from truth.
Human approval cannot be bypassed by agent tools.
advance_reason: Exceptional leverage, unusually complete evidence, and high-impact research governance concept.

one_line: A local-first data-cleaning workbench makes every agent write a human-approved diff.
what_it_does: Profiles and analyzes CSVs in-browser, proposes fixes as exact before/after diffs, and requires approval without uploading the file.
leverage_rationale: Shared in-tab state and structured read/propose/approve tools materially improve privacy, precision, and reviewability over UI-driving or remote data workflows.
leverage_evidence: About text says agent and human operate on the same JavaScript object.
Writes are proposals and exact diffs; no tool mutates the table.
Devpost screenshot shows WAITING ON YOU and AGENT ACTIVITY panels.
execution_rationale: The packet shows a coherent workbench and approval model with structured messy data, but there is no submitted video and the frame sheets are image captures rather than independently verified interaction.
execution_evidence: About text specifies profiling, queries, charts, diffs, approval, rejection, and privacy receipt.
Frames show tables, detail panels, status controls, and multiple workflow states.
Devpost demo thumbnail shows the approval rail and agent activity.
impact_rationale: Analysts handling sensitive customer, salary, or operational CSVs have a concrete privacy and cleanup problem; local reviewable automation addresses it directly.
impact_evidence: About text gives concrete messy CSV examples: inconsistent regions, currency, dates, and duplicates.
Privacy-preserving browser-only workflow is explicitly targeted at compliance-sensitive data.
creativity_rationale: Data cleaning is a known category, but the strict reads-free/writes-as-proposals contract and privacy receipt are a meaningful original angle.
creativity_evidence: Undo is deliberately not exposed as a tool; human ownership of reversals is part of the design.
Single-source shared object and approval diffs are central rather than decorative.
usability_note: Approval cards and diffs make risk legible; manual approval for every write may add workflow friction.
red_flags: No video was submitted; visual evidence is mostly repeated dashboard captures.
standouts: Strong privacy boundary and human-controlled writes.
Clear product rule: reads are free, writes are proposals.
advance_reason: Meaningful WebMCP/privacy delta with a concrete analyst workflow, though execution evidence is thinner than the top entries.

one_line: A moral decision game makes players experience how much authority to delegate to an AI agent.
what_it_does: Presents four dilemmas and MIND/HAND/HEART delegation choices, with reflection, confirmation, consequences, and a Human Balance across control dimensions.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP lets the agent act inside persistent game state and reflect on the player’s tentative choice, but a general agent could likely reproduce much of the interaction with UI access.
leverage_evidence: Pitch says the agent acts inside the live experience while final authority remains human.
About text describes persistent session state, direction-specific reflection, explicit confirmation, and consequences.
Frames show multi-step choice and confirmation screens.
execution_rationale: The frame sheets show a coherent multi-step flow and consistent visual language; no video or live run is submitted, so core agent behavior and consequence handling remain claimed.
execution_evidence: Frames show introduction, question, MIND/HAND/HEART selection, reconsideration, and final confirmation.
About text specifies four dilemmas and five Human Balance dimensions.
Demo is marked alive, but no video evidence is available.
impact_rationale: People interested in AI literacy and delegated responsibility have a credible reflective/play experience, though impact is primarily experiential rather than task utility.
impact_evidence: About text frames concrete everyday dilemmas: apology, homework, hiring shortlist, and misinformation.
Final screens explicitly preserve player responsibility.
creativity_rationale: Turning human-versus-AI authority into a playable, consequence-bearing moral experience is a fresh synthesis with a memorable interaction model.
creativity_evidence: MIND/HAND/HEART model maps delegation choices to a Human Balance rather than a morality score.
Metropolis-inspired framing supports an original story and reflective mechanic.
usability_note: Sequential prompts and confirmation/reconsideration make the intended interaction understandable.
red_flags: No video or direct agent invocation evidence in the packet.
standouts: Strong thematic alignment between mechanics and WebMCP authority boundaries.
Final decision remains explicitly human.
advance_reason: Distinctive and coherent interactive concept; agent execution needs stronger evidence in later review.

one_line: A neighborhood services marketplace combines verified identity, escrow, reputation, and conversational AI hiring.
what_it_does: Helps clients find providers, post jobs, escrow payment, release funds on approval, and lets workers list services through an AI assistant.
leverage_rationale: Conversational structured actions could simplify multi-step hiring and payment flows, but the marketplace and transaction outcomes are largely reproducible through conventional UI automation or APIs.
leverage_evidence: Pitch says AI finds providers, posts jobs, holds payment, and releases it when satisfied.
About text describes verified people, on-chain vouches, escrow, and agent-assisted listing/hiring.
Frames show AI/chat, dashboard, jobs, and service marketplace screens.
execution_rationale: The packet shows a broad coherent product concept and multiple interface surfaces, but core verification, escrow, and completed transaction behavior are marketing claims rather than demonstrated end-to-end.
execution_evidence: Devpost page presents a titled product demo and consistent trust/escrow messaging.
Frames show dashboard, jobs, AI assistant, and marketplace UI.
No video was submitted and frame text is often illegible.
impact_rationale: Trust and payment safety are real problems for local clients and freelancers; the two-sided use case is concrete and valuable if operational.
impact_evidence: About text gives personal scenarios of plumber scams and unpaid animation work.
Product targets both hiring clients and service providers with escrow and reputation.
creativity_rationale: Local services, escrow, social vouching, and conversational hiring are a fresh synthesis, though each component is familiar.
creativity_evidence: Feature set combines AI assistant, smart-contract escrow, vouching, disputes, reviews, and hyper-local map.
Blockchain is abstracted from end users.
usability_note: Conversational hiring promises simplicity, but marketplace trust and payment flows add operational complexity.
red_flags: Escrow, blockchain, verification, and guaranteed payment claims are not independently evidenced.
standouts: Addresses trust failure on both sides of local services marketplaces.
Conversational agent spans discovery, posting, and payment lifecycle.
advance_reason: Strong audience/problem fit and ambitious scope, but execution and WebMCP indispensability remain only moderately evidenced.

one_line: A bicycle photo becomes a human-confirmed visual identity for later recovery assessment.
what_it_does: Suggests bicycle specs and durable visual anchors from registration photos, compares found-bike photos, and prepares a human-reviewed recovery report.
leverage_rationale: Structured agent access supports image-derived candidates and shared human confirmation, but a general agent with image/UI access could approximate much of the flow; the strongest delta is controlled state and safe reporting.
leverage_evidence: About text describes agent suggestions, owner confirmation, later comparison, explanation, and report preparation.
Frames show staged photo-to-spec, human confirmation, and Recovery DNA creation workflows.
Pitch says nothing is sent automatically and the report is human-reviewed.
execution_rationale: The packet is coherent and shows a staged prototype workflow, but no video and no completed recovery match or report are visible.
execution_evidence: Frames show bicycle image, spec fields, progress stages, and human-confirmation screens.
Devpost screenshot embeds a titled registration-to-recovery demo.
About text specifies durable versus replaceable visual evidence.
impact_rationale: Bicycle theft/recovery and difficult model registration are real problems for owners; a reviewable object-specific identity could provide credible niche value.
impact_evidence: About text identifies owners forgetting exact model details and model names failing to distinguish changed bicycles.
Recovery report is explicitly safety-oriented and non-automatic.
creativity_rationale: The shift from model recognition to a distributed visual passport for one changing physical object is an original and memorable angle.
creativity_evidence: Frames repeatedly distinguish identity beyond a model name and recovery DNA for one object.
Durable frame evidence is separated from replaceable parts.
usability_note: Photo-first and confirmation-led flow is approachable; accuracy and review burden are unresolved.
red_flags: About text states Itta is an existing QR-based recovery service; only Recovery DNA appears to be the new layer.
No completed comparison/recovery result is visible.
standouts: Human confirmation is central to a potentially high-stakes identification workflow.
Object-specific identity handles changed parts better than model lookup.
advance_reason: Credible niche impact and original concept, with moderate evidence and a pre-existing underlying service.

one_line: A shared WebMCP workspace lets agents research menus, compare options, build carts, and complete commerce tasks.
what_it_does: Provides a human-agent bridge for direct structured interaction with websites, demonstrated through restaurant browsing and ordering.
leverage_rationale: Direct structured website capabilities can replace fragile screen scraping across research/compare/checkout steps, with the agent operating the site’s real state; however, the submission is broad and proof is packaging-only.
leverage_evidence: Pitch explicitly targets research, comparison, decisions, and complex task completion together.

About text contrasts WebMCP with visual interfaces and fragile browser automation.
execution_rationale: The concept and restaurant demo are coherent, but no frame sheets were submitted and the packet contains no video transcript; execution beyond the embedded static demo is thinly evidenced.

Screenshot visibly includes assistant prompts, menu cards, prices, and add-item controls.
No submitted video frames are available.

impact_evidence: About text uses concrete lunch-ordering decisions involving dietary needs, budget, and delivery.

creativity_rationale: The human-agent bridge is a useful synthesis and commerce demo, but the interaction is a relatively expected application of WebMCP.
creativity_evidence: Positions the website as a shared workspace rather than an agent merely clicking UI.

standouts: Clear articulation of websites as shared human-agent workspaces.
Concrete restaurant ordering surface makes the concept legible.

leverage_rationale: Structured access to architectural intent, exact regions, sketches, and native generation state is materially better than UI driving for iterative design collaboration, although the demo link is dead.

leverage_rationale: Structured game-state access is convenient and more reliable than screen reading, but a general agent can trivially drive a simple Wordle UI and achieve the same outcome.

impact_evidence: About text frames agent assistance and autonomous play as accessibility/use-case benefits.

standouts: Clear, bounded WebMCP tool surface.

one_line: A governed mission layer lets agents prepare actions while humans retain exact authority over critical effects.
what_it_does: Shapes intent into versioned missions with policies, causal modes, escalation, reversible delegation, approval gates, receipts, and audit verification.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP is used as a bounded agent surface for governance and shared mission state; human-only authority tools, version/digest binding, and receipts materially change reliability and safety versus generic UI driving.
leverage_evidence: About text describes 11 bounded tools and excludes approval/rejection/delegation/rollback from agent tools.
Mission contracts bind approval to exact intent digest, version, time, and single use.
Devpost screenshot visibly shows WAITING_APPROVAL, HUMAN DECISION REQUIRED, exact-intent approval, reject, rollback, and ratify controls.
execution_rationale: The governance model is coherent and the demo thumbnail shows mission shaping and authority states, but no video was submitted and actual execution/audit-chain verification is claimed rather than observed.
execution_evidence: Devpost screenshot shows mission shaper, operating profile, state, proposed effects, and authority controls.
About text specifies server-side validation and attributable receipts.
Facts report live demo, but no video transcript or frames.
impact_rationale: Teams using agents for releases and other consequential operations have a real need for bounded autonomy, escalation, and accountable approval; the value is credible even for a focused audience.
impact_evidence: About text gives release-readiness as a concrete mission example.
Product preserves human sovereignty over critical effects and produces receipts/audit verification.
creativity_rationale: Treating agent work as versioned governed missions with causal deliberation, exact-intent approval, and reversible effects is an original systems interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Capability is explicitly separated from authority.
Management-by-exception plus single-use digest-bound approval is a deep treatment of governance rather than a generic confirmation dialog.
usability_note: Explicit states and authority controls clarify risk, though governance terminology and mission shaping add cognitive load.
red_flags: No video submitted; live execution and audit verification are not independently observed.
standouts: Human authority is structurally excluded from agent tools.
Exact-intent, versioned, reversible approval model is unusually rigorous.
advance_reason: Strong agent-governance leverage and distinctive, credible interaction model warrant advancement despite limited video evidence.
